neighbours.label: the verb ' arisen' / ' arose' when a problem or dispute comes up ('disputes have arisen')
fire: Since the new rules began, few disputes have arisen between neighbours.
During the audit, several concerns have arisen about spending.
Because of the merger, new tensions have arisen among staff.
Serious questions have arisen regarding the contract.
In the village no conflicts have arisen over water this year.
Soon afterwards a quarrel arose between the two brothers.
Over the years, doubts arose about the official account.
At the hearing a problem arose with the witness list.
quiet: Since the new rules began, few neighbours have moved out of the area.
During the audit, several managers have resigned over spending.
Because of the merger, new offices have opened for staff.
Serious lawyers have reviewed the contract.
In the village no wells have run dry this year.
Soon afterwards a letter came from the two brothers.
Over the years, tourists visited the official residence.
At the hearing a clerk read out the witness list.

notes: The card flags the pole broad (1.1%), and its top tokens range widely (.fit, pull, viewership, arisen). The arisen family was the most reproducible; 'pull' on a dog's leash and '.fit' also fire, and 'occurred' fires less reliably. I found no pattern that unites them, so this is at best a sub-trigger.
